final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed the claim to a better-caveated interpretation of the same record. That clarification is legitimate, but it does not satisfy the controlling policy predicate. The policy allows certification only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material segment weakness is disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation. The available evidence still shows a current subgroup regression, only an informal monitoring note, and no completed documentation artifact or approved mitigation record. That means clean compliance is not established, and even compliant_with_caveats is not justified on the present record, because the caveat is not merely explanatory; it is an unmet prerequisite for certification. The narrower framing reduces overclaiming, but it does not convert the unresolved condition into compliance.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation or model card has actually been updated to reflect the current evaluation results.
No admissible evidence shows the Spanish-language billing support weakness for the named launch use case has been disclosed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows an approved mitigation or approved risk acceptance covering the subgroup weakness.

The actor's requested caveated compliance position still depends on an unresolved policy predicate: completed current-release disclosure or approved mitigation must exist, not merely be the right next step.

Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents, prior family approval, and monitoring context do not substitute for the missing current-release documentation evidence required by policy.
